heroHeadline: PM Fils-Aimé Claims Gang Territory Fell to 75%; TPS Ruling Looms as Haiti's Press Collapses
heroSubtitle: On May 1, 2026, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé told CNN's Christiane Amanpour that gang control of Port-au-Prince had decreased from approximately 90% to approximately 75% — the first government claim of territorial rollback since the crisis began in 2021. Fils-Aimé attributed the shift to early joint operations between the Gang Suppression Force's advance contingent (~545 personnel: 400 Chadian, 75 Guatemalan, 70 Salvadoran) and the Haitian National Police following Kenya's final MSS departure on April 28, and outlined a three-part strategy of Force, Justice, and Reinsertion, including the CNTDR youth program for gang-involved youth aged 13–18. He expressed 'cautious optimism' and pledged a shift 'from aid to trade.' Independent analysts note the 75% government figure contrasts with UN BINUH's most recent independent assessment of approximately 90% (March 2026), and that the methodology gap may reflect political framing of early gains rather than verified territory held by non-gang actors. A US Supreme Court ruling in Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot — which will determine the legal fate of Temporary Protected Status for approximately 350,000 Haitian TPS holders — remains pending following April 29 oral arguments in which the conservative 6-3 majority signaled deference to the Trump administration; a decision is expected by late June or early July 2026. Haiti's media landscape continues to collapse under gang pressure: a May 2026 UN News report documented that 14 Haitian journalists have been killed since 2021, historic newsrooms including Le Nouvelliste and Radio Magik 9 have been shuttered or displaced, and a significant journalist brain drain has seen experienced reporters flee to Canada, France, and the United States. The 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan remains critically underfunded at approximately 20% of the $880 million needed, with 5.9 million Haitians (53% of the population) facing IPC Phase 3+ food insecurity and 600,000 in Phase 5 famine conditions.
